summary.text: For \(n=9\), the product of the first nine primes is \(223092870\), and its associated term is \(223092870^2+1=49770428644836901=29^2\cdot59180057841661\). Thus this term is not squarefree, so the squarefreeness assertion—and hence the conjunction—fails, independently of the infinitude claim.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
P_n=\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}p_k,
\]
where \(p_0=2,p_1=3,p_2=5,\ldots\) are the primes in increasing order. The sequence in question is
\[
a(n)=P_n^2+1.
\]
The conjecture is a conjunction: first, that every \(a(n)\) is squarefree, and second, that \(a(n)\) is prime for infinitely many \(n\). It is enough to disprove the first assertion, since a conjunction is false whenever either one of its components is false.

We use \(n=9\). The first nine primes, with indexing beginning at \(0\), are
\[
2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,23.
\]
Consequently
\[
P_9=2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13\cdot17\cdot19\cdot23.
\]
Multiplying successively gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
2\cdot3&=6,\\
6\cdot5&=30,\\
30\cdot7&=210,\\
210\cdot11&=2310,\\
2310\cdot13&=30030,\\
30030\cdot17&=510510,\\
510510\cdot19&=9699690,\\
9699690\cdot23&=223092870.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\[
P_9=223092870
\]
and hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
a(9)
 &=223092870^2+1\\
 &=49{,}770{,}428{,}644{,}836{,}901.
\end{aligned}
\]
This number has a nontrivial square divisor. Indeed,
\[
29^2=841
\]
and direct multiplication gives
\[
49{,}770{,}428{,}644{,}836{,}901
 =841\cdot59{,}180{,}057{,}841{,}661.
\]
Therefore
\[
29^2\mid a(9).
\]

For completeness, the same divisibility can also be seen before carrying out the final large multiplication. Modulo \(841=29^2\), the primorial satisfies
\[
223092870\equiv800\equiv-41\pmod{841}.
\]
Therefore
\[
P_9^2+1\equiv(-41)^2+1=1682=2\cdot841\equiv0\pmod{841},
\]
again showing that \(29^2\mid a(9)\).

A positive integer is squarefree only if no square of a nonunit integer divides it. Equivalently, if \(x^2\mid m\) and \(m\) is squarefree, then \(x\) must be a unit. The only unit in the natural numbers is \(1\). Applying this criterion to \(m=a(9)\) and \(x=29\), the divisibility \(29^2\mid a(9)\) would force \(29\) to be a unit. But \(29\ne1\), so \(29\) is not a unit. Hence \(a(9)\) is not squarefree.

Thus the universal assertion that every term \(a(n)\) is squarefree is false. It follows that the conjunction
\[
\bigl(\forall n,\ a(n)\text{ is squarefree}\bigr)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\bigl(\text{there are infinitely many }n\text{ for which }a(n)\text{ is prime}\bigr)
\]
is false, irrespective of the truth or falsity of its second component. This disproves the stated conjecture.
